newsitem.title: JAPAN: S.Korea says economy set for another take-off - Kang.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea says economy set for another take-off - Kang.

text.p: The South Korean economy is set for another take-off as structural reforms accelerate, Finance Minister Kang Kyong-shik said on Monday.

Speaking on the second day of the 30th annual meeting of the Asian Development Bank (ADB), Kang said that although South Korea had lagged behind changes in the international environment, resulting in sluggish growth and a widening current account deficit, it was tackling those problems.

"Although economic restructuring always entails some unpleasantness, I firmly believe (South) Korea's ongoing reforms will set the stage for another economic take-off," Kang, who is also deputy prime minister, said in a speech to the ADB.
He said the South Korean government was taking steps to further liberalise financial markets, such as encouraging the establishment of venture businesses.
Kang also said Seoul hoped the ADB would give due consideration to North Korea's desire to become a member of the 56-member bank.
"By becoming a member of the international community, North Korea would end its isolation. This alone would contribute significantly to the political and economic stablity of East Asia," he said.
The meeting, which opened on Sunday in this southern Japanese city and runs until Tuesday, will not address the issue of North Korea's membership, ADB officials said.
